title: When afraid
hook: Allah is enough for us, the best protector (3:173)
tomorrow: why would washing your face end a fight?

segments.voice: Yesterday, when waiting is long: Ya'qub's beautiful patience, weeping and still searching. Today, the waiting breaks, at two in the morning.

A phone lights up at two in the morning, and before anyone answers, your body already knows. Then the drive: empty roads, every red light too long, a grandmother in the back seat with her hands folded. What do you say in a car like that? A story answers with one short line, said in two different fires. The first fire is real wood and real flame, and a man is being thrown into it.
screen: `A PHONE AT 2 A.M.` → `EVERY RED LIGHT TOO LONG.` → `ONE LINE, TWO FIRES.`

segments.voice: The man is Ibrahim. He has broken his people's idols, and they build a fire for him. Ibn 'Abbas says, in Sahih al-Bukhari, that as Ibrahim was thrown in, his words were: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil. Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to trust. In the Qur'an, the fire is told to be coolness and peace for him. The second fire is fear. The Prophet's companions have just come through a battle, wounded and worn out, and word arrives: the people have gathered against you, so fear them. In the Qur'an's telling, the threat only increased their faith, and they said, in Pickthall's words: "Allah is Sufficient for us! Most Excellent is He in whom we trust!" The same line, Ibn 'Abbas says, the Prophet ﷺ and his companions said that day. Notice what it doesn't do. It doesn't call the danger fake. Ibrahim was really in a fire; the companions were really hurt. It answers the other thing fear says: you are alone with this, and it's too big. The line says: He is enough. And in a car at two in the morning, it's something to say when there's nothing else to say.
screen: `IBRAHIM, THROWN IN THE FIRE.` · `WOUNDED, AND TOLD TO FEAR.` · `ALLAH IS SUFFICIENT FOR US.` · `THE DANGER IS REAL. SO IS ENOUGH.` · then, large: `HE IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Say the line softly, at the pace of your breath: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil. Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to trust. Let it come a little slower each time, until the words and the breath move together. If you don't pray, say it in English, or just hold the word enough.
When afraid: the fear is real, and so is the line. Allah is enough for us, said in the fire, and said on the road.
Your line: He is enough. The danger doesn't have to shrink for that to be true. Go gently.

howItsDone: In fear or danger, many Muslims say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil (Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to trust), from Qur'an 3:173, alongside du'a and practical steps.

myth: saying hasbunallah means pretending the danger isn't real
Ibrahim was really in a fire; the companions were really wounded. the line says what's enough.

fork.setup: your little sister has a speech tomorrow and is terrified. she asks if being scared means she doesn't trust God. what fits the story?
options: no: the companions were wounded and afraid, and still said Allah is enough.
yes: if she really trusted God, she wouldn't feel scared at all.
a speech is too small a thing to bring God into; just practice it.
fork.reveal: the line was said in the middle of real danger, not after it passed. fear and trust sat in the same people.

original.note: Arabic: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to trust (3:173).

trapdoor: what you thought: a line for after the fear is gone.
what it means: a line for the middle of fear: Allah is enough for us, the best to trust.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's report from Ibn 'Abbas: Ibrahim said it in the fire, and the Prophet and his companions when told the people had gathered (3:173).
guess: fear held with the words: Allah is enough for us
fear as proof that your faith has failed
a fear you're meant to hide from others

chat.says: 2am. hospital called, Khala Samina's in ICU. dad's driving us. hands shaking. what do i even say?
options: say it with Dadi: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil. it doesn't deny the fear; He's enough.
tell Dadi everything will definitely be fine, so she stays calm on the drive.
fear means weak faith, so push it away and think about something else.
chat.meaning: Ibrahim in the fire and the wounded companions both said Allah is enough for us. The line doesn't deny danger; it answers the fear of being alone.

Ibn 'Abbas.meaning: a cousin of the Prophet who passed on his sayings

hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil.meaning: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to trust

sources.quoted: Allah is Sufficient for us! Most Excellent is He in whom we trust!

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4563 (Ibn 'Abbas: Ibrahim said 'hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil' when thrown into the fire, and Muhammad said it when told the people had gathered)
